01 / HOW IT WORKS

Come in. Try something.
Leave nothing behind.

Give a friend a Linux shell, test a script, or run a workshop.
Every session starts from the same clean image.

01

You SSH in.

Your usual SSH client. No Docker install needed on the connecting machine.

ssh -p 2222 anyone@your-server
02

A container starts.

A fresh Alpine shell, wired to your terminal. History, colors, resize, and vi work.

docker run --rm -it alpine:latest
03

You leave. It goes.

Exit or drop the connection. sshbox stops and removes that session’s container.

exit → container removed

02 / GET STARTED

Small setup.
Full shell.

Run the binary on a machine with Docker.
Connect from anywhere that can reach it.

Read the configuration docs ↗
1

Start Docker on your machine.

docker info
2

Extract your download and run sshbox.

./bin/sshbox
3

Open another terminal. Connect.

ssh -p 2222 anyone@localhost

Needs Go 1.23 or later and a running Docker daemon. Cloning gets the latest development version; release downloads are tagged builds.

git clone https://github.com/kknxzz/sshbox
cd sshbox
go run .

Then connect from another terminal:

ssh -p 2222 anyone@localhost

Any username or password works. Press Enter at the password prompt.

!
A shell for people you trust.

sshbox has no authentication. Put it behind Tailscale, a VPN, or a bastion. Don’t expose it directly to the internet. Containers have no network by default, with 256 MiB of memory and half a CPU. Container isolation isn’t a hardened security boundary.

04 / A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

Before you SSH in.

Why not just use docker run --rm?+

For a local shell, that works. sshbox adds the SSH listener, starts a separate container for each remote session, handles the terminal, and cleans up when the connection ends. The connecting person only needs an SSH client.

Can I use a different Linux image?+

Yes. Run sshbox --image ubuntu:latest, or set image in config.toml. The image needs a shell at /bin/sh, or you can choose one with --shell. Alpine is the default.

Can I install packages or access the internet?+

Networking is off by default. Start sshbox with --network bridge to allow normal Docker networking, then use the image’s package manager, such as apk add curl in Alpine. Installed packages disappear with the container.

Does anything survive a session?+

The container filesystem doesn’t. sshbox keeps its host key so server identity stays stable. If the operator enables session recording, those logs are kept on the host. Recording is off by default.
